title: Count how many files of each type a folder contains
summary: Walk through a folder, take the ending of each file name such as jpg or txt, count how many files have each ending, and list the most common types first. Useful to see what a messy download folder is full of.

aliases.text: how many files of each type in folder
count file types in directory command line
what kinds of files are in this folder
сколько файлов каждого типа в папке linux
какие типы файлов в папке и сколько

steps.explain: find lists every file under DIR. sed keeps only the text after the last dot and prints it; files without a dot print nothing. sort groups equal endings, uniq -c counts them and sort -nr lists the biggest count first. Upper and lower case count separately.
steps.cmd: find <DIR> -type f | sed -n 's/.*\.\([^./]*\)$/\1/p' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr
steps.expect: Lines such as '  42 jpg': the number of files first, then the ending.

steps.explain: Count the files that have one given ending. The pattern is quoted so the shell does not expand it. wc -l counts the lines, one per file.
steps.expect: A single number, the count of files with that ending.
